title: Bitsy — progress toward PyTorch parity (v0.2 skeleton)
subtitle: Oracle: PyTorch CUDA fp32 on GTX 1660 Super. Baseline numbers from the pre-skeleton history; this branch is documentation only.
footer: Numeric parity is achieved on the implemented subset; speed parity (ratio >= 1.00) is the open goal. Green = pass/done, amber = numeric-only, grey = pending.

groups.name: Model numerics vs PyTorch (MLP, CNN, RNN, LSTM, GPT-2)
Ops at >= 1.0x PyTorch speed (baseline: 0 of 12: elementwise x5, matmul, sqrt, gelu, softmax, reduce, CE, sgd)
Models at >= 1.0x PyTorch speed (baseline ratios: MLP ~0.46, CNN n/a, RNN 0.15, LSTM 0.04, GPT-2 0.58)
Core line budget used (target 4096; baseline legacy 5710, v0.2 plan 2850)
Roadmap phases complete (0 research; 1 skeleton; 2 lazy+parity; 3 speed; 4 release)

notes.numeric_pass_rule: max_abs_diff within documented tolerance (EXACT for simple elementwise, 1e-5 matmul/transcendental, 1e-3 model loss)
notes.speed_pass_rule: torch_ms / bitsy_ms >= 1.00 on this GPU, warmup + median + spread + clock logged
notes.baseline_source: Published tables in main:docs/PROGRESS.md and main:BENCHMARKS.md (numeric diffs and speed ratios). Live JSON reports in benchmarks/results/*.json are regenerated per run and their timing spreads drift, so the published tables are treated as canonical.
